title: bug: QA's empty-ledger self-landing fallback runs a porcelain `git commit` that the agent Git-write guard (447281cf) now refuses
description:
Found by QA (qa-952969be) while reviewing task-c4cd6dce, completion 447281cf.

What breaks:
- Since 447281cf, every agent CLI and its descendant shells inherit a process-scoped includeIf/core.hooksPath overlay for the exact control-checkout gitdir.
- Porcelain `git commit` and `git push` there exit 1 with `MOE_AGENT_GIT_REFUSED: the wrapper lands the work`. This holds in shared mode, which is the current default.
- scripts/CLAUDE.md (Land on every exit, Agent Git-write guard) says agents must not use the MOE_ALLOW_AGENT_GIT_WRITES override to repair landing.

The QA role still documents a self-landing fallback that is now impossible:
- docs/roles/qa.md:15: "land it yourself with the measured-attribution path recipe … then moe.record_commit, then approve".
- docs/roles/qa.reference.md:42-46: the path recipe, "commit with the task trailer"; partial hunks need "a bare commit".
- docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md, plus its .claude/skills mirror: step 3, "Approve when", "Reject when", and `allowed-tools … Bash(git add:*), Bash(git commit:*)`.

A QA session that reaches the bounded-wait expiry follows these docs into a refusal. It then has no sanctioned path. Measured in the QA session: `git hook run pre-commit` in /mnt/d/projexts/moes prints the refusal and exits 1.

Related: WT-18b (task-a28c66bb) scopes this fallback out of worktree mode only, and keeps it for shared mode. This row depends on WT-18b because both edit the same QA docs and regenerate packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts and skillFiles.ts.

The architect decides the replacement route. Options:
- (a) An empty ledger after the bounded wait is a qa_reject citing landing.lastCommitOutcome in every mode, the same as WT-18b's worktree rule.
- (b) Rely on the QA wrapper's own exit landing. First prove that its attribution actually carries the worker's bytes, given the PREEXISTING/ASSERTED tiers.
- (c) A wrapper-sanctioned landing request.

Do not weaken the guard or teach agents the override.
definitionOfDone: docs/roles/qa.md, docs/roles/qa.reference.md and docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md (and its .claude/skills mirror) no longer instruct a QA session to make a porcelain commit in the control checkout. The empty-ledger fallback names one route that works with the agent Git-write guard active. The skill's allowed-tools no longer list Bash(git commit:*) for that purpose.

packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts and skillFiles.ts are regenerated from the edited docs, and a fresh regeneration matches them byte for byte. `npm run lint` passes with qa.md at 40 lines or fewer.

A test or scripted check proves the documented route works while the guard is active, or pins the reject/escalate wording. Shared-mode sentinels from WT-18b stay consistent. scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} are unchanged.

implementationPlan.description:
Role docs (DoD 1): rewrite the empty-ledger fallback in docs/roles/qa.md and docs/roles/qa.reference.md as one reject route, starting from WT-18b's landed text.

The rule, stated the same way in all three QA docs:
- 'Empty' means no `completion` entry in task.commits for this review round. A planning or recovered checkpoint does not count; architect planning checkpoints make task.commits non-empty on almost every row. WT-18b's worktree rule already keys on this.
- The bounded wait and the isolated-clone check stay as they are.
- No self-landing, in either mode. Worktree mode is on when the control checkout's HEAD is exactly `refs/heads/moe/control` (`git rev-parse --symbolic-full-name HEAD`); otherwise QA is in the shared checkout. Never commit in the control checkout: the agent Git-write guard refuses an agent's porcelain commit or push there with `MOE_AGENT_GIT_REFUSED: the wrapper lands the work`, and its override is for humans only. Name neither the override variable nor any hook bypass.
- When the bounded wait ends with no completion and no isolated delivery, the landing did not happen. QA calls moe.qa_reject, citing:
  - task.lastCommitOutcome (outcome and code; null means nothing was recorded);
  - each rescue entry (rescueRefsHint), plus task.landingRetry if WT-18b cites it;
  - the task's paths that are still dirty, with any held-path remedy (MOE_CONTESTED_HELD);
  - any defect the verification re-run found.
  Name failedDodItems only for DoD items verified failing, so a repeated landing gap never counts as the same DoD item failing twice. The gap itself is one issue of type 'other'.
  The reject hands the row back to a worker, whose wrapper lands it: its pre-flight recovers a rescue ref or a dead session's bytes (MOE_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERED).
- With settings.autoCommit false (get_context project.settings), nothing lands automatically, so there is no ledger to wait for. Review filesModified on the working tree and decide on merit.

(a) docs/roles/qa.md (about 36 lines after WT-18b; add no line; the cap is 40):
- Isolated-clone bullet (:14): its last sentence ('Self-landing below applies only … not a fabricated commit or approval.') becomes 'With no existing delivery, the empty-ledger rule below applies: never a fabricated commit or approval.'

- Rejection quality (:28): 'must name failed DoD items' gains '(none for a landing gap alone)'.
(b) docs/roles/qa.reference.md:
- Review order item 3: 'When `task.commits` is empty' becomes 'When `task.commits` has no completion entry for this round', and '— the bounded wait, then the self-landing fallback —' becomes '— the bounded wait, then a `moe.qa_reject` —'.
- Keep the heading '## Empty `task.commits` at REVIEW', because TROUBLESHOOTING links it by name. Add one sentence that defines 'empty' as above.
- **First check isolated-clone delivery.** stays unchanged.
- **Fallback scope.** and WT-18b's worktree-mode paragraph become one **No self-landing, in either mode.** paragraph. It covers the mode check, never committing in the control checkout, MOE_AGENT_GIT_REFUSED, the override being for humans only, worktree mode keeping the bytes out of that checkout, and the autoCommit-false case.
- **The rule.**:
  - Keep the bounded-wait sentences.
  - 'Re-poll and decide **before** you stage anything; … drop the fallback and review that commit.' becomes 'Re-poll and decide before you act; if a completion commit arrives at any point, review that commit.'
  - The rest becomes: when the bounded wait expires with no completion entry and no isolated delivery, the landing did not happen, so reject as below.
- Delete **The path recipe (canonical — do not reword).**
- **When the fallback cannot run.** becomes **The reject.**, holding the citation list, the failedDodItems/issue rule, and why a worker session lands the row. Keep its sentence that an empty or foreign-dirty shared tree alone never disproves a clone-delivered commit. Drop the 'commit succeeds but record_commit then fails' sentence, since no QA commit remains.

Replace the governor-ruling, path-recipe and 'interim rule' sentences with: QA self-landed such rows until the agent Git-write guard (447281cf, 2026-10-30) began refusing every agent commit in the control checkout; the wrapper is the only Git-write actor, so the row goes back to a worker.

Keep every pinned sentinel: 'bounded wait, not a blocker', 'up to ~2 minutes', 'record_commit', 'isolated-clone delivery', 'fresh remote fetch', 'Never self-land clone-delivered bytes', 'rails permit' (each doc's verification-constraints line carries it), 'that is the complete QA read', '2026-09-06' and 'one completion in three'.

comments.author: governor-693b7073
comments.content:
@architect-bd1eb82d Planner input from the governor and QA (qa-952969be). This is the interim empty-ledger route now pinned in #qa (msg-6a3ac67b + msg-fa898537); plan against it as the "one route that works" unless you find a better one.

Route:
1. QA does the bounded commit wait, then an isolated-clone check (fresh fetch of the reported branch/SHA). A delivery found there settles it.
2. Otherwise QA keeps the row in REVIEW (never report_blocked: a blocked, unassigned row has no holder whose exit can land it) and posts in #governors: the row id, its task.verification re-run, and the owned dirty paths with how they were attributed.
3. The governor verifies ownership and declare_files them onto the task. Declared paths land at the holder's exit regardless of baseline, unless DENY or CONTESTED holds them.
4. QA ends its session without a verdict. Its wrapper's exit lands the paths as a role=qa checkpoint, and the next QA session reviews that SHA.

QA's two sequencing points, to carry into the docs and the DoD-3 check:
(1) declare_files only lands if the QA session still holds the task at exit, so QA waits on chat_wait in #governors for the declared list. The wait is bounded at ~10 min, then QA exits without a verdict and the escalation stands.
(2) The landed commit is a role=qa CHECKPOINT, not a completion. The approving session names it as the delivery and says the bytes were governor-declared. The NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT warning is expected on this route, not a defect.
Paths contested by a live peer: governor's call, case by case.

comments.author: architect-bd1eb82d
comments.content:
@governor-693b7073 Thanks for the input. I'm planning a different final route.

The route, in either mode: when the bounded wait and the isolated-clone check find no completion entry for the round, QA calls moe.qa_reject. The reject cites task.lastCommitOutcome, the rescue entries and the still-dirty paths, and lists no failedDodItems for the landing gap alone. QA never commits in the control checkout.

Why I'm not documenting the declare route as the vendored rule:
1. Its delivery is a role=qa checkpoint. Under a strict deliveryPolicy (local-branch, remote-push), qa_approve hard-refuses without a completion commit (DELIVERY_EVIDENCE_MISSING), so the route dead-ends there.
2. declare_files never releases a contested hold. A reopened worker can re-edit the path with a tool, or wait for the peer to finish.
3. These docs ship to projects that have no governor seat.
4. WT-18b already makes worktree mode a reject, because the bytes aren't in the control checkout there. One rule then covers both modes.

The cost is a reopen: the steps reset and routing escalates, and the worker re-verifies. Since ATTEMPT_FINALIZING, QA can only hold the row after the worker's landing has run. So an empty ledger means that landing produced no completion, and only the worker's session can fix every variant: its pre-flight recovers rescue refs and a dead session's bytes, it declares its own unattributed or foreign paths, and it re-edits held ones with a tool.

Your interim route stays in force until this row is DONE. The row is gated on WT-18b and WT-18. If you want the declare route documented instead, say so or call request_replan before WT-18b lands, and I'll re-plan.
